You are performing PHASE 1 (audit only) of a full redesign of the Nxeon customer portal. READ-ONLY investigation of a LIVE PRODUCTION codebase.

HARD RULES: Repo /opt/nxeon — ONLY Read/Grep/Glob/ls. NEVER edit/create/delete/move anything under /opt/nxeon; NEVER run npm/npx/prisma/build/db/service/git-write commands. Do not touch /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. The ONLY file you may write: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/report-backend-games-hosting.md
Read the brief first: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/brief-full.md (sections 01, 02, 23, 24, 26, 34, 56, 57, 59, 73, 76 most relevant).

MISSION: COMPLETE CAPABILITY INVENTORY (so nothing gets lost) for these product areas, each as its own section:

A. GAME SERVERS (paid): lib/actions-games.ts, lib/actions-game-control.ts, lib/actions-game-config.ts, lib/actions-gameplans.ts, lib/actions-mods.ts, lib/game-order.ts, lib/game-meta* / game catalog (the 19+ games list and per-game metadata: slugs, art, presets, ports, mod support), worker handlers for game provisioning, prisma models (GamePlan, game server fields on Server, mods, schedules?), app/dashboard/games/**, components/customer/games/** or wherever the game control panel lives (console/RCON, files, mods/plugins, backups, players, worlds, commands, history, schedules, settings, activity, custom domain via lib/custom-domain-dns.ts, SFTP access, public server directory via lib/actions-community.ts / app/(marketing)/servers/[subdomain]).
B. FREE MINECRAFT TIER: lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts, lib/actions-freemc-*.ts (inventory, mods, public, roles, worlds), lib/free-minecraft-control.ts, lib/freemc-capacity.ts, app/dashboard/free-minecraft, components/customer/freemc/** and FreeMinecraftPanel/Loader — every capability (create, game types/modes, presets, power, console/RCON, players, settings, roles/LuckPerms, inventory editor, mod menu, worlds, rename, change subdomain, public listing, sleep/wake behavior, capacity limits).
C. SHARED HOSTING: lib/actions-hosting.ts (2000+ lines — be thorough), lib/actions-hosting-db.ts, lib/hosting.ts, worker/hosting.ts, prisma HostingAccount/HostingTask and related, app/dashboard/hosting/**, components/customer/hosting/** — overview, websites, files, databases, domains/subdomains/addon domains, email, apps (one-click installers incl. WordPress), PHP switch, cron, backups/restore, SSL, settings, suspend/renew, the ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING flag status.
D. SITES / WEBSITES (app/dashboard/sites, lib/actions-sites.ts) vs VPS "Websites & PHP" vs hosting websites — clarify what each is (this is a known concept overlap).
E. VOLUMES / BLOCK STORAGE: lib/actions-volumes.ts, app/dashboard/volumes — create/attach/detach/resize/delete/billing.
F. NXCLOUD: lib/actions-nxcloud.ts, app/dashboard/nxcloud — what is it, capabilities, custom domain.
G. MIGRATION CENTER: lib/actions-migrate.ts (large), worker/migrate*.ts, app/dashboard/migrate/** incl. /consolidate — the whole flow (probe → plan → run → remediation/portal remediation → cutover/pointMigrationDns → finishMigrationSetup), states, what the customer sees at each step.
H. BUILD / AI: app/dashboard/build, app/dashboard/claude-code, app/dashboard/projects, lib/actions-claude*.ts, components/customer/claude-code/** (Matrix, MatrixProvider, multi-console), lib/actions-tokens.ts if API tokens relate — what exists, what's gated (Anthropic key), what states.

For EACH area deliver: (1) capability table: capability | action/API | inputs | guards | states | where exposed in UI today (file) | gaps; (2) state model (status enums, job stages actually observable, polling/streaming) — precise enough to build truthful provisioning/progress UI; (3) DEPLOY-TIME vs LATER: which attributes must be chosen before payment/provisioning vs changeable afterwards (e.g., game type switch, world reset, plan resize, region move?, hosting domain attach, WordPress install); (4) hidden/flag-gated capabilities.

Write the report file, then return a ~300-word summary + the report path.

1	You are working on the complete redesign of the Nxeon customer portal.
2	
3	This is NOT a cosmetic redesign.
4	
5	This is a full product-level UI/UX transformation and visual identity overhaul of the entire customer-facing Nxeon platform.
6	
7	The existing portal has been developed incrementally over many months by continuously adding features on top of previous features. As a result, there is significant inconsistency across navigation, layouts, spacing, components, typography, forms, cards, buttons, flows, visual hierarchy, terminology, asset usage, and overall UX.
8	
9	Your job is to establish a completely new, coherent Nxeon design system and then migrate the entire portal into that system.
10	
11	The result should feel like a premium, venture-backed, multi-million-dollar infrastructure / AI / cloud technology company.
12	
13	It must NOT feel like a generic SaaS dashboard.
14	It must NOT feel like a typical Claude-generated application.
15	It must NOT feel "vibecoded."
16	It must NOT simply copy Vercel, Linear, DigitalOcean, Cloudflare, Stripe, or any other existing product.
17	
18	Nxeon needs its OWN visual identity.
19	
20	==================================================
21	01. CRITICAL NON-NEGOTIABLE CONSTRAINT
22	==================================================
23	
24	DO NOT CHANGE THE BACKEND.
25	
26	This redesign is primarily a frontend architecture, UI, UX, interaction, visual identity, and information architecture project.
27	
28	Preserve:
29	
30	- Existing backend functionality
31	- Existing APIs
32	- Existing API contracts
33	- Existing database behavior
34	- Existing provisioning logic
35	- Existing billing logic
36	- Existing authentication
37	- Existing server operations
38	- Existing hosting operations
39	- Existing domain functionality
40	- Existing mailbox functionality
41	- Existing DNS functionality
42	- Existing game server functionality
43	- Existing VPS functionality
44	- Existing shared hosting functionality
45	- Existing payment processing
46	- Existing subscription logic
47	- Existing account logic
48	- Existing support functionality
49	- Existing permissions
50	- Existing team functionality
51	- Existing infrastructure integrations
52	- Existing server controls
53	- Existing one-click installers
54	- Existing provisioning systems
55	- Existing server lifecycle operations
56	
57	Do not remove functionality simply because it is not visible in the screenshots.
58	
59	There are many screens, states, flows, modals, drawers, forms, dialogs, server-management operations, mailbox operations, DNS operations, billing flows, and deployment workflows that are NOT represented in the supplied screenshots.
60	
61	The redesign must account for the entire existing application.
62	
63	Before changing code, audit the existing codebase thoroughly.
64	
65	Understand:
66	
67	1. Every major route.
68	2. Every page.
69	3. Every reusable component.
70	4. Every modal.
71	5. Every drawer.
72	6. Every form.
73	7. Every API interaction.
74	8. Every server action.
75	9. Every deployment flow.
76	10. Every checkout flow.
77	11. Every billing flow.
78	12. Every domain flow.
79	13. Every email/mailbox flow.
80	14. Every hosting flow.
81	15. Every game-server flow.
82	16. Every VPS flow.
83	17. Every settings flow.
84	18. Every empty/loading/error/success state.
85	19. Every responsive/mobile behavior.
86	20. Every existing asset.
87	
88	Do not assume the screenshots represent the complete application.
89	
90	The screenshots are evidence of the current design problems.
91	
92	They are NOT visual references to copy.
93	
94	==================================================
95	02. FIRST STEP — AUDIT BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION
96	==================================================
97	
98	Before making major visual changes, inspect the repository.
99	
100	Map the existing product architecture.
101	
102	Create an internal understanding of:
103	
104	- Current routing
105	- Page hierarchy
106	- Product hierarchy
107	- Navigation
108	- Components
109	- Data dependencies
110	- State management
111	- Backend/API dependencies
112	- Existing design tokens
113	- Existing CSS
114	- Existing Tailwind configuration if applicable
115	- Existing component library
116	- Existing icons
117	- Existing images
118	- Existing SVGs
119	- Existing animations
120	- Existing loading states
121	- Existing form components
122	
123	Identify duplicated UI patterns.
124	
125	Identify inconsistent UI patterns.
126	
127	Identify components that are visually similar but implemented separately.
128	
129	Identify components that should become shared primitives.
130	
131	Identify pages that currently behave differently despite representing similar concepts.
132	
133	DO NOT immediately start changing random pages.
134	
135	First establish the new system.
136	
137	==================================================
138	03. THE NEW NXEON PRODUCT IDENTITY
139	==================================================
140	
141	The new Nxeon identity should communicate:
142	
143	- Infrastructure
144	- Reliability
145	- Intelligence
146	- Speed
147	- Precision
148	- Technology
149	- Trust
150	- Premium quality
151	- Modern cloud computing
152	- Automation
153	- Simplicity
154	- Control
155	
156	The visual identity should feel like:
157	
158	"Enterprise-grade infrastructure presented through an exceptionally refined consumer/developer experience."
159	
160	Think:
161	
162	Deep atmospheric navy
163	+
164	Precision typography
165	+
166	Subtle luminous technology
167	+
168	Premium surfaces
169	+
170	Intelligent motion
171	+
172	High information density without visual clutter
173	+
174	Exceptional hierarchy
175	+
176	Purposeful visual details
177	
178	Avoid:
179	
180	- Generic purple SaaS gradients everywhere
181	- Excessive glassmorphism
182	- Huge rounded cards everywhere
183	- Random glowing blobs
184	- Stock AI imagery
185	- Generic 3D illustrations
186	- Excessive gradients

188	- Excessive shadows
189	- Excessive border boxes

193	- Copying competitor layouts

311	==================================================
312	06. TYPOGRAPHY
313	==================================================
314	
315	Typography needs to become significantly more premium.
316	
317	Avoid oversized generic SaaS headings.
318	
319	Use typography to create hierarchy.
320	
321	The interface should feel compact and intelligent.
322

324

328	- precise labels

1599	/// claim row is inserted in the SAME transaction as the resource row it names, so

1	/**
2	 * Per-game customization schema (MVP).
3	 *
4	 * A plain module (NO "use server") so it can be imported from server components,
5	 * "use server" action files AND the worker daemon alike — it holds no secrets and
6	 * performs no I/O.
7	 *
8	 * It declares, per game family, the available server *variants* (the loader/flavour
9	 * a player runs — Paper vs Vanilla, Carbon vs Oxide, …) and a versioned list of
10	 * *settings fields* that drive a dynamic UI. Fields are intentionally limited to
11	 * the handful of options players actually change, keyed on the game's own real
12	 * config keys (server.properties, PalWorldSettings.ini, cvars, …) — no invented
13	 * cvars — so a future real "apply" step can render them 1:1.
14	 *
15	 * Exports: `familyFor`, `schemaFor`, `validateConfig` plus the `GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`
16	 * table and its types.
17	 */
18	
19	/** Bump when the field set changes in a way the worker/apply step must notice. */
20	export const GAME_CONFIG_VERSION = 1;
21	
22	export type FieldType = "enum" | "bool" | "int" | "string";
23	
24	/**
25	 * When a setting takes effect:
26	 *  - "deploy": needs a server restart / redeploy (world seed, tickrate, …)
27	 *  - "live":   can be pushed to a running server (motd, pvp, max players, …)
28	 * MVP treats both the same (simulated apply) but the UI surfaces the distinction.
29	 */

31	
32	export type ConfigField = {

34	  key: string;

44	  max?: number;

888	 * customization schema exists for it, else null.

891	  if (!server) return null;

909	export type ValidateResult =
910	  | { ok: true; values: Record<string, string | number | boolean> }
911	  | { ok: false; error: string };
912	
913	/**
914	 * Validate & coerce a settings object against a family's field schema. Unknown
915	 * keys are dropped; missing keys fall back to the field default. Returns a clean,
916	 * fully-populated values object ready to persist to `Server.gameConfig`.
917	 */
918	export function validateConfig(
919	  family: string,
920	  values: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined
921	): ValidateResult {
922	  const schema = GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS[family];
923	  if (!schema) return { ok: false, error: `Unknown game family "${family}".` };
924	
925	  const input = values ?? {};
926	  const out: Record<string, string | number | boolean> = {};
927	
928	  for (const field of schema.fields) {
929	    const raw = input[field.key];
930	    const provided = raw !== undefined && raw !== null;
931	
932	    switch (field.type) {
933	      case "bool": {
934	        out[field.key] = provided ? raw === true || raw === "true" || raw === "on" : (field.default as boolean);
935	        break;
936	      }
937	      case "int": {
938	        let n = provided ? Number(raw) : (field.default as number);
939	        if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} must be a number.` };
940	        n = Math.trunc(n);
941	        if (field.min !== undefined && n < field.min)
942	          return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} must be at least ${field.min}.` };
943	        if (field.max !== undefined && n > field.max)
944	          return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} must be at most ${field.max}.` };
945	        out[field.key] = n;
946	        break;
947	      }
948	      case "enum": {
949	        const v = provided ? String(raw) : String(field.default);
950	        if (!field.options?.some((o) => o.value === v))
951	          return { ok: false, error: `Invalid value for ${field.label}.` };
952	        out[field.key] = v;
953	        break;
954	      }
955	      case "string": {
956	        const v = provided ? String(raw) : String(field.default);
957	        if (field.required && v.trim().length === 0) {
958	          return {
959	            ok: false,
960	            error: `${field.label} is required.${field.help ? ` ${field.help}` : ""}`,
961	          };
962	        }
963	        if (v.length > 256) return { ok: false, error: `${field.label} is too long (max 256 chars).` };
964	        // CONFIG INJECTION: these values are written verbatim into LINE-ORIENTED
965	        // files on the customer's VM by worker/game-config.ts —
966	        // `server.properties` (`motd=<value>`), Rust's `server.cfg`
967	        // (`server.hostname "<value>"`) and Valheim's launch-args file. A newline
968	        // therefore does not set one option, it appends arbitrary further
969	        // options: a motd of "hi\nenable-rcon=true\nrcon.password=x" turns RCON
970	        // on with a chosen password, and that password is then read back out of
971	        // the same file and interpolated into an `mcrcon` command line.
972	        // `enum`/`int`/`bool` are constrained by their own branches; `string` was
973	        // the only field type with no allowlist at all, so it is checked here —
974	        // at the one point every caller (UI, server action and worker re-validation)
975	        // already goes through.
976	        // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
977	        if (/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(v)) {
978	          return {
979	            ok: false,
980	            error: `${field.label} may not contain line breaks or control characters.`,
981	          };
982	        }
983	        out[field.key] = v;
984	        break;
985	      }
986	    }
987	  }
988	
989	  return { ok: true, values: out };
990	}

2	 * Game server control panel — SSH/RCON transport + per-family control facts.
3	 *
4	 * A plain server-side module (NO "use server", no client imports). Imported by
5	 * BOTH the server actions (lib/actions-game-control.ts) and the worker
6	 * (worker/game-control.ts). It NEVER runs in the browser — the customer's root
7	 * credentials and their server's RCON password stay on our server.
8	 *
9	 * Everything here operates on the CUSTOMER'S OWN game VM over the platform's
10	 * existing SSH (host/port/root-password derived exactly like lib/sftp.ts, reused
11	 * via lib/ssh-exec.ts `withServerSsh`). Two transport rules, mirroring the rest of
12	 * the control panel:
13	 *
14	 *   1. STRICT ALLOWLIST VALIDATION for anything that reaches a shell. Ports, unit
15	 *      names, paths and file names are validated/allowlisted or rejected — never
16	 *      sanitized. Family/unit hints are compile-time constants, never customer
17	 *      input.
18	 *
19	 *   2. RCON never touches a shell at all. We read the server's RCON port/password
20	 *      out of its own config file, then open a TCP channel to 127.0.0.1:<port> on
21	 *      the game VM THROUGH the SSH connection (`conn.forwardOut`) and speak the
22	 *      Source RCON wire protocol directly. The RCON port is never exposed off the
23	 *      box, the password is only ever a protocol packet body (not an argv token),
24	 *      and the customer's console command is validated to be single-line/control-
25	 *      char-free before it is sent.
26	 *
27	 * SANDBOX: callers gate real SSH behind `!SANDBOX`; on staging the inline reads
28	 * return realistic synthetic data so the whole UX works without a live VM.
29	 */

359	 * Returns a 1..65535 integer or null — the parsed number, never the caller's text,
360	 * so it is safe by construction rather than by escaping.

362	export function parsePort(raw: unknown): number | null {

369	 * A single RCON/console command line typed by the customer. Their own server, so
370	 * the verb set is intentionally open — but it is sent as a Source RCON packet body
371	 * (never a shell), and we still forbid NUL/newline/control chars (which would forge
372	 * multiple packets or corrupt framing) and bound the length.
373	 */
374	export function validateRconCommand(raw: string): { ok: true; command: string } | { ok: false; error: string } {
375	  const c = String(raw ?? "");
376	  if (c.trim().length === 0) return { ok: false, error: "Enter a command." };
377	  if (c.length > 512) return { ok: false, error: "Command is too long (max 512 chars)." };
378	  // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
379	  if (/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(c)) return { ok: false, error: "Command may not contain line breaks or control characters." };
380	  return { ok: true, command: c.trim() };

409	/**
410	 * Locate the first existing file: explicit candidates via `test -f`, then a
411	 * bounded `find` over `roots`. Candidate paths are compile-time constants; the
412	 * returned hit is re-validated against the path allowlist before any caller uses
413	 * it. Returns null when nothing matches.
414	 */
415	export async function remoteLocateFile(
416	  conn: Client,
417	  candidates: string[],
418	  roots: string[],
419	  name: string
420	): Promise<string | null> {
421	  const testExpr = candidates.map((p) => `if [ -f ${shq(p)} ]; then echo ${shq(p)}; exit 0; fi;`).join(" ");
422	  const findExpr = roots.length
423	    ? `for r in ${roots.map((r) => shq(r)).join(" ")}; do [ -d "$r" ] && find "$r" -maxdepth 6 -type f -name ${shq(name)} 2>/dev/null | head -1; done | head -1`
424	    : "true";
425	  const { stdout } = await exec(conn, `${testExpr} ${findExpr}`, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
426	  const hit = stdout
427	    .split(/\r?\n/)
428	    .map((s) => s.trim())
429	    .find((s) => s.length > 0);
430	  return hit && isSafeRemotePath(hit) ? hit : null;
431	}

434	export async function remoteLocateDir(conn: Client, candidates: string[]): Promise<string | null> {
435	  const expr = candidates.map((p) => `if [ -d ${shq(p)} ]; then echo ${shq(p)}; exit 0; fi;`).join(" ");
436	  const { stdout } = await exec(conn, expr, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
437	  const hit = stdout
438	    .split(/\r?\n/)
439	    .map((s) => s.trim())
440	    .find((s) => s.length > 0);
441	  return hit && isSafeRemotePath(hit) ? hit : null;
442	}

444	/** Read a small remote text file (or null). Uses `cat`, capped by head. */
445	async function readRemoteText(conn: Client, path: string): Promise<string | null> {
446	  if (!isSafeRemotePath(path)) return null;
447	  const { stdout, code } = await exec(conn, `cat ${shq(path)} 2>/dev/null | head -c 65536`, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
448	  if (code !== 0 && stdout.length === 0) return null;
449	  return stdout;
450	}

452	/** Parse a `key=value` / `key value` config into a lowercase-keyed map. */
453	function parseFlatConfig(text: string): Record<string, string> {
454	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
455	  for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
456	    const t = line.trim();
457	    if (!t || t.startsWith("#") || t.startsWith("//") || t.startsWith("!") || t.startsWith(";")) continue;
458	    let key: string;
459	    let val: string;
460	    const eq = t.indexOf("=");
461	    if (eq >= 0) {
462	      key = t.slice(0, eq).trim();
463	      val = t.slice(eq + 1).trim();
464	    } else {
465	      const sp = t.search(/\s/);
466	      if (sp < 0) continue;
467	      key = t.slice(0, sp).trim();
468	      val = t.slice(sp + 1).trim();
469	    }
470	    // Strip surrounding quotes.
471	    val = val.replace(/^"(.*)"$/, "$1").replace(/^'(.*)'$/, "$1");
472	    if (key) out[key.toLowerCase()] = val;
473	  }
474	  return out;
475	}

477	/** Pull `Key=Value` pairs out of Palworld's `OptionSettings=(...)` blob. */
478	function parsePalworldIni(text: string): Record<string, string> {
479	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
480	  const idx = text.indexOf("OptionSettings=(");
481	  const open = idx >= 0 ? text.indexOf("(", idx) : -1;
482	  const close = open >= 0 ? text.indexOf(")", open) : -1;
483	  if (open < 0 || close < 0) return out;
484	  const inner = text.slice(open + 1, close);
485	  let cur = "";
486	  let inQuote = false;
487	  const pairs: string[] = [];
488	  for (const ch of inner) {
489	    if (ch === '"') inQuote = !inQuote;
490	    if (ch === "," && !inQuote) {
491	      pairs.push(cur);
492	      cur = "";
493	    } else cur += ch;
494	  }
495	  if (cur) pairs.push(cur);
496	  for (const p of pairs) {
497	    const eq = p.indexOf("=");
498	    if (eq < 0) continue;
499	    let v = p.slice(eq + 1).trim();
500	    v = v.replace(/^"(.*)"$/, "$1");
501	    out[p.slice(0, eq).trim().toLowerCase()] = v;
502	  }
503	  return out;
504	}

506	export type RconCreds =
507	  | { ok: true; port: number; password: string }
508	  | { ok: false; reason: string };

510	/**
511	 * Read a game server's RCON credentials out of its own config file, over SSH.
512	 * The password is used ONLY as a Source RCON packet body downstream — never a
513	 * shell argument — and the port is parsed to an integer (`parsePort`), so neither
514	 * value can inject anywhere.
515	 */
516	export async function readRconCreds(conn: Client, spec: GameControlSpec): Promise<RconCreds> {
517	  const cfg = spec.rconConfig;
518	  if (spec.rcon !== "source" || !cfg) {
519	    return { ok: false, reason: `Remote console is not available for ${spec.label}.` };
520	  }
521	  const path = await remoteLocateFile(conn, cfg.candidates, cfg.findRoots, cfg.findName);
522	  if (!path) return { ok: false, reason: `Could not find ${spec.label}'s config file to read RCON settings.` };
523	  const text = await readRemoteText(conn, path);
524	  if (text == null) return { ok: false, reason: `Could not read ${spec.label}'s config file.` };
525	
526	  const map = cfg.kind === "palworld-ini" ? parsePalworldIni(text) : parseFlatConfig(text);
527	
528	  if (cfg.enableKey) {
529	    const en = (map[cfg.enableKey.toLowerCase()] ?? "").toLowerCase();
530	    if (en !== "true" && en !== "1" && en !== "on") {
531	      return { ok: false, reason: `RCON is not enabled in ${spec.label}'s config — enable it and restart to use the console.` };
532	    }
533	  }
534	  const password = map[cfg.passwordKey.toLowerCase()] ?? "";
535	  if (!password) return { ok: false, reason: `No RCON password is set in ${spec.label}'s config.` };
536	  if (password.length > 256) return { ok: false, reason: "RCON password in the config looks malformed." };
537	
538	  const port = cfg.portKey ? parsePort(map[cfg.portKey.toLowerCase()]) ?? cfg.defaultPort : cfg.defaultPort;
539	  return { ok: true, port, password };
540	}

542	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
543	// Source RCON over an SSH-forwarded TCP channel
544	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
545	
546	const RCON_TYPE_AUTH = 3;
547	const RCON_TYPE_EXEC = 2;
548	const RCON_TYPE_RESPONSE = 0;
549	const RCON_ID_AUTH = 0x1;
550	const RCON_ID_CMD = 0x2;
551	const RCON_ID_END = 0x2711; // sentinel id for the trailing empty packet
552	
553	function rconPacket(id: number, type: number, body: string): Buffer {
554	  const bodyBuf = Buffer.from(body, "ascii");
555	  const buf = Buffer.alloc(bodyBuf.length + 14);
556	  buf.writeInt32LE(bodyBuf.length + 10, 0); // size = id(4)+type(4)+body+2 nulls
557	  buf.writeInt32LE(id, 4);
558	  buf.writeInt32LE(type, 8);
559	  bodyBuf.copy(buf, 12);
560	  // two trailing NUL bytes already zero from Buffer.alloc
561	  return buf;
562	}

564	/**
565	 * Open a TCP channel to `host:port` on the game VM THROUGH the authenticated SSH
566	 * connection. The RCON port therefore never needs to be reachable off the box.
567	 */
568	export function forwardTcp(conn: Client, host: string, port: number, timeoutMs = 8000): Promise<Duplex> {
569	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
570	    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error("Timed out opening RCON channel")), timeoutMs);
571	    conn.forwardOut("127.0.0.1", 0, host, port, (err, stream) => {
572	      clearTimeout(timer);
573	      if (err) return reject(err);
574	      resolve(stream as unknown as Duplex);
575	    });
576	  });
577	}
578	
579	export type RconResult = { ok: true; response: string } | { ok: false; error: string };
580	
581	/**
582	 * Speak Source RCON over `stream`: authenticate, run `command`, and read the
583	 * (possibly multi-packet) response, using a trailing empty packet as the
584	 * end-of-response sentinel. Never throws — resolves an {ok,error} result. The
585	 * password is only ever a packet body; the command was validated by the caller.
586	 */
587	export function sourceRcon(stream: Duplex, password: string, command: string, timeoutMs = 8000): Promise<RconResult> {
588	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
589	    let acc = Buffer.alloc(0);
590	    let authed = false;
591	    let response = "";
592	    let done = false;
593	
594	    const finish = (r: RconResult) => {
595	      if (done) return;
596	      done = true;
597	      clearTimeout(timer);
598	      try {
599	        stream.end();
600	      } catch {
601	        /* best effort */
602	      }
603	      resolve(r);
604	    };
605	    const timer = setTimeout(
606	      () => finish(authed ? { ok: true, response } : { ok: false, error: "RCON timed out (no response)." }),
607	      timeoutMs
608	    );
609	
610	    stream.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => {
611	      acc = Buffer.concat([acc, chunk]);
612	      while (acc.length >= 4) {
613	        const size = acc.readInt32LE(0);
614	        if (size < 10 || size > 4110) return finish({ ok: false, error: "Malformed RCON response." });
615	        if (acc.length < size + 4) break;
616	        const id = acc.readInt32LE(4);
617	        const type = acc.readInt32LE(8);
618	        const body = acc.slice(12, 4 + size - 2).toString("ascii");
619	        acc = acc.slice(4 + size);
620	
621	        if (!authed) {
622	          // The auth response is a type-2 (AUTH_RESPONSE) packet; id === -1 on failure.
623	          if (type === RCON_TYPE_EXEC) {
624	            if (id === -1) return finish({ ok: false, error: "RCON authentication failed (wrong password)." });
625	            authed = true;
626	            stream.write(rconPacket(RCON_ID_CMD, RCON_TYPE_EXEC, command));
627	            stream.write(rconPacket(RCON_ID_END, RCON_TYPE_EXEC, "")); // sentinel
628	          }
629	          // A leading empty RESPONSE_VALUE some servers send pre-auth is ignored.
630	        } else {
631	          if (id === RCON_ID_END) return finish({ ok: true, response });
632	          if (type === RCON_TYPE_RESPONSE) response += body;
633	        }
634	      }
635	    });
636	    stream.on("error", (e: Error) => finish({ ok: false, error: e?.message || "RCON connection error." }));
637	    stream.on("close", () => finish(authed ? { ok: true, response } : { ok: false, error: "RCON connection closed." }));
638	
639	    stream.write(rconPacket(RCON_ID_AUTH, RCON_TYPE_AUTH, password));
640	  });
641	}

643	/**
644	 * Full inline RCON round-trip on an already-open SSH connection: read creds from
645	 * the server's config, tunnel to 127.0.0.1:<port>, run one command. Callers guard
646	 * SANDBOX and ownership before reaching here.
647	 */
648	export async function runRcon(conn: Client, spec: GameControlSpec, command: string): Promise<RconResult> {
649	  const creds = await readRconCreds(conn, spec);
650	  if (!creds.ok) return { ok: false, error: creds.reason };
651	  let stream: Duplex;
652	  try {
653	    stream = await forwardTcp(conn, "127.0.0.1", creds.port);
654	  } catch (e) {
655	    return { ok: false, error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Could not open RCON channel." };
656	  }
657	  return sourceRcon(stream, creds.password, command);
658	}

667	export type LogResult = { ok: true; lines: string[]; unit: string | null } | { ok: false; error: string };
668	
669	/**
670	 * Tail the game service's recent logs. Resolves the unit from the family hints
671	 * (compile-time constants), then reads the last `n` journal lines; if journald has
672	 * nothing, falls back to a `.log` file under the data roots. Read-only.
673	 */
674	export async function readGameLogs(conn: Client, spec: GameControlSpec, n = 200): Promise<LogResult> {
675	  const lines = Math.min(Math.max(Math.trunc(n) || 200, 20), 500);
676	  const hints = spec.serviceHints.map(shq).join(" ");
677	  const roots = spec.dataRoots.map(shq).join(" ");
678	  const script = [
679	    `unit=""`,
680	    `for c in ${hints}; do systemctl cat "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { unit="$c"; break; }; done`,
681	    `if [ -z "$unit" ]; then unit=$(systemctl list-units --type=service --plain --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -i ${shq(spec.family)} | head -1 | awk '{print $1}'); fi`,
682	    `echo "NXLOG:UNIT:${"$"}{unit:-none}"`,
683	    `if [ -n "$unit" ]; then journalctl -u "$unit" -n ${lines} --no-pager 2>/dev/null; fi`,
684	    // Fallback: newest *.log under the data roots (bounded).
685	    `f=""; for r in ${roots}; do [ -d "$r" ] && f=$(find "$r" -maxdepth 4 -type f -name '*.log' 2>/dev/null | head -1) && [ -n "$f" ] && break; done`,
686	    `if [ -n "$f" ]; then echo "NXLOG:FILE:$f"; tail -n ${lines} "$f" 2>/dev/null; fi`,
687	  ].join("\n");
688	  const { stdout } = await exec(conn, script, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
689	  const all = stdout.split(/\r?\n/);
690	  let unit: string | null = null;
691	  const out: string[] = [];
692	  for (const l of all) {
693	    const m = /^NXLOG:UNIT:(.*)$/.exec(l);
694	    if (m) {
695	      unit = m[1] === "none" ? null : m[1];
696	      continue;
697	    }
698	    if (/^NXLOG:FILE:/.test(l)) continue;
699	    out.push(l);
700	  }
701	  while (out.length && out[out.length - 1].trim() === "") out.pop();
702	  return { ok: true, lines: out.slice(-lines), unit };
703	}

705	export type WorldEntry = { name: string; sizeBytes: number; isDir: boolean };
706	export type WorldResult = { ok: true; dir: string | null; entries: WorldEntry[] } | { ok: false; error: string };

708	/** List the top-level world/save entries with sizes. Read-only. */
709	export async function readWorlds(conn: Client, spec: GameControlSpec): Promise<WorldResult> {
710	  const dir = await remoteLocateDir(conn, spec.dataRoots);
711	  if (!dir) return { ok: true, dir: null, entries: [] };
712	  // `du -sb` on each top-level entry: size<TAB>path. Bounded to 200 entries.
713	  const script =
714	    `cd ${shq(dir)} 2>/dev/null || exit 0; ` +
715	    `for e in * .*; do [ "$e" = "." ] || [ "$e" = ".." ] && continue; [ -e "$e" ] || continue; ` +
716	    `t=f; [ -d "$e" ] && t=d; sz=$(du -sb "$e" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1); printf '%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n' "$t" "${"$"}{sz:-0}" "$e"; done | head -200`;
717	  const { stdout } = await exec(conn, script, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
718	  const entries: WorldEntry[] = [];
719	  for (const line of stdout.split(/\r?\n/)) {
720	    const parts = line.split("\t");
721	    if (parts.length < 3) continue;
722	    const [t, sz, ...rest] = parts;
723	    const name = rest.join("\t").trim();
724	    if (!name) continue;
725	    entries.push({ name, sizeBytes: Number(sz) || 0, isDir: t === "d" });
726	  }
727	  return { ok: true, dir, entries };
728	}

737	    `for f in "$d"/*.tar.gz; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; ` +
738	    `sz=$(stat -c '%s' "$f" 2>/dev/null); mt=$(stat -c '%Y' "$f" 2>/dev/null); ` +
739	    `printf '%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n' "${"$"}{sz:-0}" "${"$"}{mt:-0}" "$f"; done | head -100`;
740	  const { stdout } = await exec(conn, script, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
741	  const backups: BackupEntry[] = [];
742	  for (const line of stdout.split(/\r?\n/)) {
743	    const parts = line.split("\t");
744	    if (parts.length < 3) continue;
745	    const path = parts.slice(2).join("\t").trim();
746	    if (!path || !isSafeRemotePath(path)) continue;
747	    backups.push({
748	      name: path.split("/").pop() || path,
749	      path,
750	      sizeBytes: Number(parts[0]) || 0,
751	      modifiedMs: (Number(parts[1]) || 0) * 1000,
752	    });
753	  }
754	  backups.sort((a, b) => b.modifiedMs - a.modifiedMs);
755	  return { ok: true, backups };
756	}

758	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
759	// Player-list parsing (from RCON responses)
760	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
761	
762	export type Player = { name: string; extra?: string };
763	
764	/**
765	 * Parse the connected-player list out of a family's list-command RCON response.
766	 * Best-effort per family; unknown shapes return the raw response so the UI can
767	 * still show it.
768	 */
769	export function parsePlayers(family: GameFamily, response: string): { players: Player[]; raw: string } {
770	  const raw = response.trim();
771	  if (family === "minecraft") {
772	    // Strip ANSI escape codes — Paper/Spigot embed color codes in RCON responses.
773	    const clean = raw.replace(/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/g, "");
774	    // Vanilla: "There are 2 of a max of 20 players online: Alice, Bob"
775	    const m1 = /players online:\s*(.+)$/im.exec(clean);
776	    if (m1) {
777	      const names = m1[1].split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
778	      return { players: names.map((name) => ({ name })), raw };
779	    }
780	    // Paper: "There are 2 out of maximum 20 players online.\ndefault: Alice, Bob"
781	    const m2 = /players online\.\s*\n.*?:\s*(.+)$/im.exec(clean);
782	    if (m2) {
783	      const names = m2[1].split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
784	      return { players: names.map((name) => ({ name })), raw };
785	    }
786	    return { players: [], raw };
787	  }
788	  if (family === "palworld") {
789	    // "name,playeruid,steamid" lines, first line is a header.
790	    const lines = raw.split(/\r?\n/).map((l) => l.trim()).filter(Boolean);
791	    const players: Player[] = [];
792	    for (const l of lines) {
793	      if (/^name\s*,/i.test(l)) continue;
794	      const cols = l.split(",");
795	      if (cols[0]) players.push({ name: cols[0].trim(), extra: cols.slice(1).join(",").trim() || undefined });
796	    }
797	    return { players, raw };
798	  }
799	  // cs2 `status` and anything else: hand back the raw block.
800	  return { players: [], raw };
801	}

5	/**
6	 * True when `sub` is free to claim across BOTH the free and paid Minecraft
7	 * subdomain namespaces (`FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain`
8	 * live in different tables but resolve under the same `play.nxeon.cloud` zone,
9	 * so a name taken in either one is unavailable in both). `excludeServerId`/
10	 * `excludeFreeMcId` let a rename check availability without tripping over the
11	 * row's own current value.
12	 *
13	 * Server-only (imports `./db`) — a client component must import
14	 * ./game-subdomain-rules directly for the format check instead.
15	 */
16	export async function isSubdomainAvailable(
17	  sub: string,
18	  opts?: { excludeServerId?: string; excludeFreeMcId?: string },
19	): Promise<boolean> {
20	  const [freeHit, paidHit] = await Promise.all([
21	    db.freeMinecraftServer.findFirst({
22	      where: { subdomain: sub, ...(opts?.excludeFreeMcId ? { id: { not: opts.excludeFreeMcId } } : {}) },
23	      select: { id: true },
24	    }),
25	    db.server.findFirst({
26	      where: { subdomain: sub, ...(opts?.excludeServerId ? { id: { not: opts.excludeServerId } } : {}) },
27	      select: { id: true },
28	    }),
29	  ]);
30	  return !freeHit && !paidHit;
31	}

137	/** Slider ceiling per family: 5x the largest tier actually sold today, floored at
138	 *  50 so even a small-roster game (e.g. The Forest, seeded up to 8) still offers a
139	 *  meaningfully bigger custom option. */
140	export function playerSliderMax(family: GameFamily): number {
141	  const c = GAME_PLAYER_CURVES[family];
142	  return Math.max(50, c.maxSeededSlots * 5);
143	}

145	/**
146	 * Recommended cpu/ram/disk for a given player count on this family — a
147	 * DEFAULT-SETTER for the custom-spec sliders, never a hard floor or ceiling
148	 * itself (the caller clamps into the actual custom-plan floor/ceiling).
149	 */
150	export function recommendedSpecForPlayers(family: GameFamily, players: number): GameResourceSpec {
151	  const c = GAME_PLAYER_CURVES[family];
152	  const p = Math.max(1, Math.round(players));
153	  const ramMB = Math.max(512, Math.round((c.ramBaseMB + c.ramPerPlayerMB * p) / 256) * 256);
154	  const cpuCores = Math.max(1, Math.round(c.cpuBaseCores + c.cpuPerPlayer * p));
155	  const diskGB = Math.max(5, Math.round(c.diskBaseGB + c.diskPerPlayerGB * p));
156	  return { cpuCores, ramMB, diskGB };
157	}

1	/**
2	 * Inject `-e TYPE=<VARIANT>` into a Minecraft OsTemplate's setupScript from
3	 * `Server.gameVariant` (the customer's checkout choice — vanilla/paper/purpur/
4	 * fabric/forge, see lib/game-config.ts's MINECRAFT.variants).
5	 *
6	 * Found live 2026-08-30: this substitution never existed anywhere in the
7	 * provisioning pipeline. The OsTemplate's setupScript is one static string
8	 * with no `TYPE` at all, so `gameVariant` was captured at checkout, stored on
9	 * `Server`, and then completely ignored — every Minecraft customer got plain
10	 * Vanilla regardless of what they picked (or paid for a plugin-support tier
11	 * and had their manually-installed plugins never load, since Vanilla has no
12	 * plugin API at all). Diagnosed via a real customer ticket: the fix here is
13	 * minecraft-specific by design (it's the only family with a real variant
14	 * concept today) — generalize via `schemaFor(family)` if another family gains
15	 * one, rather than hardcoding a second family name here.
16	 *
17	 * Explicit and idempotent: always injects a `TYPE`, even for "vanilla" —
18	 * removes any reliance on the image's own default ever staying Vanilla — and
19	 * is a no-op if the script already names an explicit `TYPE` (never override
20	 * something a future per-family script sets on purpose).
21	 *
22	 * Kept in its own side-effect-free module (rather than inline in
23	 * worker/index.ts) so it can be unit tested directly — importing
24	 * worker/index.ts runs its top-level `main()` job-polling loop.
25	 */
26	import { schemaFor } from "../lib/game-config";
27	
28	export function applyGameVariant(setupScript: string, family: string | null, variant: string | null): string {
29	  if (family !== "minecraft") return setupScript;
30	  if (!variant) return setupScript;
31	  if (/-e\s+TYPE=/.test(setupScript)) return setupScript;
32	  const type = variant.toUpperCase();
33	  return setupScript.replace(/(docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b)/, `$1 -e TYPE=${type}`);
34	}
35	
36	/**
37	 * The generalization this file's own docstring called for: substitute a
38	 * customer's checkout-time `Server.gameConfig` values into an OsTemplate's
39	 * setupScript, for whichever fields already appear in it as a docker
40	 * `-e KEY=...` env-var placeholder.
41	 *
42	 * Found live 2026-08-31 auditing DST (`dst` family): the whole per-family
43	 * customization schema in lib/game-config.ts (`ConfigField`, one per
44	 * `docker run -e KEY=...` in prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts and its Wave 1-3
45	 * predecessors) is captured at checkout into `Server.gameConfig`
46	 * (lib/game-order.ts) and shown in the post-deploy Settings tab, but — same
47	 * root cause as `applyGameVariant` above, just never generalized —
48	 * `provision()` in worker/index.ts never read it. Every family's setup
49	 * script always ran with its hardcoded static default (usually `''`),
50	 * regardless of what the customer entered at checkout. For most fields that
51	 * meant a cosmetically-wrong default (wrong MOTD, wrong hostname string);
52	 * for DST's `TOKEN` (an online DST cluster refuses to start with none — see
53	 * lib/game-config.ts's DST schema comment) it meant the container never
54	 * bound its port at all and PROVISION's own `checkGamePortOpen` health check
55	 * would time out and hard-fail the customer's paid order.
56	 *
57	 * Deliberately conservative: ONLY touches a key if the setupScript already
58	 * declares it as `-e KEY=...` — fields with no such placeholder (e.g. DST's
59	 * `PASSWORD`, which the yeetzone image never wired to an env var at all) are
60	 * left untouched rather than guessing a docker flag that isn't there.
61	 * Values are re-quoted as a single-quoted shell literal with proper `'`
62	 * escaping (`'\''`) so a customer-supplied string can never break out of the
63	 * quote and inject shell — the same safety property `validateConfig`'s own
64	 * control-character guard exists for, just extended to this second consumer
65	 * (a `docker run` command line) since the injection surface differs from a
66	 * line-oriented remote config file.
67	 */
68	export function applyGameConfigEnv(
69	  setupScript: string,
70	  family: string | null,
71	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined,
72	): string {
73	  if (!family || !gameConfig) return setupScript;
74	  const schema = schemaFor(family);
75	  if (!schema) return setupScript;
76	  let out = setupScript;
77	  for (const field of schema.fields) {
78	    const raw = gameConfig[field.key];
79	    if (raw === undefined || raw === null) continue;
80	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${field.key}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
81	    if (!re.test(out)) continue; // this field isn't docker-env-driven in this script — leave it alone
82	    const escaped = String(raw).replace(/'/g, `'\\''`);
83	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${field.key}='${escaped}'`);
84	  }
85	  return out;
86	}

1	/**
2	 * Real (not cosmetic) "what's actually happening right now" progress labels for
3	 * <ProvisioningOverlay/>, for both Shared Hosting and VPS/game-server orders.
4	 *
5	 * The provisioning workers (worker/hosting.ts, worker/index.ts) run in a SEPARATE
6	 * process from the web app (nxeon-worker.service vs nxeon-web.service), so an
7	 * in-memory signal (like lib/chat-bot-step.ts's TTL map, which works because the
8	 * chat bot and the poll route share one process) is not visible here — the signal
9	 * has to be durable. `HostingAccount.provisioningStep` / `Server.provisioningStep`
10	 * are those durable, best-effort columns: the worker writes a short human label
11	 * between real, observable command groups, and this module reads it back. A null
12	 * step means "no real signal yet" — callers fall back to generic/cosmetic text
13	 * rather than claiming false precision.
14	 *
15	 * For Shared Hosting specifically, "real progress" continues past the account
16	 * going ACTIVE: a one-click app install (WordPress, etc.) queued at order time
17	 * runs as a `HostingTask` AFTER the account is active, and that queue already has
18	 * genuine DB-persisted status transitions (PENDING → RUNNING → DONE/FAILED) — no
19	 * new instrumentation needed there, just a kind → label mapping.
20	 */
21	
22	import { db } from "./db";
23	
24	const HOSTING_TASK_LABELS: Record<string, string> = {
25	  WORDPRESS_INSTALL: "Installing WordPress…",
26	  APP_INSTALL: "Installing your application…",
27	  PHP_SWITCH: "Switching PHP version…",
28	  BACKUP: "Creating a backup…",
29	  RESTORE: "Restoring your backup…",
30	  CREATE_SUBDOMAIN: "Setting up your subdomain…",
31	  DELETE_SUBDOMAIN: "Removing your subdomain…",
32	  CREATE_ADDON_DOMAIN: "Connecting your domain…",
33	  DELETE_ADDON_DOMAIN: "Removing your domain…",
34	  CREATE_CRON: "Scheduling your cron job…",
35	  DELETE_CRON: "Removing your cron job…",
36	  INSTALL_DBTOOL: "Installing the database manager…",
37	  ENSURE_DBMGR: "Preparing your database manager…",
38	  APPLY_PLAN_LIMITS: "Applying your new plan…",
39	  RESET_DB_PASSWORD: "Resetting your database password…",
40	  SET_PRIMARY_DOMAIN: "Switching your primary domain…",
41	};
42	
43	/**
44	 * The real step label for a Shared Hosting account, or null if there's nothing
45	 * genuine to say right now.
46	 *
47	 *  - PENDING/PROVISIONING: the account's own `provisioningStep` column, or a
48	 *    generic fallback if the worker hasn't written one yet (e.g. SANDBOX mode,
49	 *    which completes before any step is ever recorded).
50	 *  - ACTIVE: the label for whichever content task (WordPress/app install, PHP
51	 *    switch, …) is PENDING or RUNNING for this account, if any. This is what
52	 *    lets <ProvisioningOverlay/> keep showing progress through a post-order
53	 *    WordPress install even though the account itself is already ACTIVE.
54	 *  - Anything else (SUSPENDED/FAILED/DELETING, or ACTIVE with no live task):
55	 *    null.
56	 */
57	export async function hostingProvisioningStep(accountId: string): Promise<string | null> {
58	  const account = await db.hostingAccount.findUnique({
59	    where: { id: accountId },
60	    select: { status: true, provisioningStep: true },
61	  });
62	  if (!account) return null;
63	  if (account.status === "PENDING" || account.status === "PROVISIONING") {
64	    return account.provisioningStep || "Setting up your hosting account…";
65	  }
66	  if (account.status === "ACTIVE") {
67	    const task = await db.hostingTask.findFirst({
68	      where: { accountId, status: { in: ["PENDING", "RUNNING"] } },
69	      orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" },
70	      select: { kind: true },
71	    });
72	    if (task) return HOSTING_TASK_LABELS[task.kind] ?? "Finishing setup…";
73	  }
74	  return null;
75	}

77	/**
78	 * The real step label for a VPS/game-server order, or null. Only meaningful while
79	 * PENDING/PROVISIONING/REINSTALLING — worker/index.ts's provision() writes
80	 * `Server.provisioningStep` between its real, observable checkpoints (clone,
81	 * configure, start, guest-agent boot, SSH reachable, and — for game orders only —
82	 * the game's own port opening). A null return (no column value yet) means the
83	 * job hasn't reached its first checkpoint, or this deployment predates the
84	 * column; callers fall back to the existing cosmetic cycling text rather than
85	 * inventing a label for a phase we can't actually observe.
86	 */
87	export async function serverProvisioningStep(serverId: string): Promise<string | null> {
88	  const server = await db.server.findUnique({
89	    where: { id: serverId },
90	    select: { status: true, provisioningStep: true },
91	  });
92	  if (!server) return null;
93	  if (!["PENDING", "PROVISIONING", "REINSTALLING"].includes(server.status)) return null;
94	  return server.provisioningStep || null;
95	}
